ca_luther_spires_2.blurb: A cluster of spires on a ridge above Luther Pass, south of Lake Tahoe, at roughly 7,400 to 7,900 feet. This section holds ten routes, a mix of bolted lines and gear climbs, with a handful of top-rope options too. Grades run from 5.7 up to 5.11, but the bulk sit in the 5.10 range, so it suits climbers comfortable on moderate leads. The spires are still being developed and the rock is mostly sturdy, though fresh routes can shed the odd loose flake. Getting here takes a real uphill hike on the Tahoe Rim Trail, so expect a workout before you rope up.
ca_luther_spires_2.approach: Follow the Tahoe Rim Trail from the trailhead, cross the footbridge, then take the left fork that switchbacks steeply uphill to the base of the spires.

ca_oceanside_boulders.blurb: A small set of large sandstone boulders on the Del Norte coast, just beside the Promontory wall and sitting at sea level. Ten routes mix bolted lines, gear climbs and top-ropes, with several hanging out over the surf. Grades span roughly 5.6 to 5.11, with most falling between 5.6 and 5.10, so there are warm-ups as well as a few testing lines. Some scrambling is needed to reach certain blocks, though most are easy to walk up to. It makes a quick add-on to a day at Promontory rather than a destination of its own.

ca_9_secor.blurb: A small quartzite wall of about 45 to 65 feet in the Silver Lake cliffs above June Lake, at around 7,400 feet. Ten routes, half bolted and half set up for top-roping, run from about 5.4 to 5.8, making it a gentle spot for beginners and families. The face looks east-northeast. Rock here is loose in places and the wall sees little traffic, so wear a helmet and keep belayers well back from the base. Several lines link into the neighbouring wall, which allows longer outings.
ca_9_secor.approach: From the Silver Lake parking lot, hike up to the base of the sector 7 cliff, then continue northwest beyond the low end of the Moynier wall to Secor.

ca_aspen_boulder.blurb: A single granite boulder among aspens in Lee Vining Canyon on the Eastern Sierra, around 7,400 feet and a half-minute walk from where you leave the car. It is the standout of the local bouldering, with problems on all four sides and flat landings. Ten problems cover a wide spread, from very easy up to V8, with a cluster of mid-grade lines around V2 to V4, a V7 sit start and the hard arete at the top end. Good for a short session or as a stop alongside other canyon boulders.

ca_beach_wall.blurb: A small bouldering wall high on Mount Rubidoux in Riverside, a little south of the main Beach Boulder. It offers ten easy problems, from the very easiest up to about V1, and the ones I could confirm are short, around 15 feet. Landings are flat, since the problems sit just above road level. That makes it a friendly place to warm up, bring beginners or get in some mileage before heading to the harder boulders on the hill. It is reached by walking uphill, with the wall on the west side close to the top.

ca_big_baldy.blurb: A granite dome inside Kings Canyon National Park, around 8,000 feet, with views toward the Great Western Divide. Most of the ten routes here are crack climbs, with a few knob and slab lines, and almost all are traditional. Grades run from about 5.6 to the low 5.12s, with a big share in the 5.10 range, plus one aid line. The rock is good, though little-travelled cracks can hold lichen or moss. The dome rarely gets crowded, and the hike in is long enough to keep it quiet. Snow on the approach can matter in winter.

ca_brown_corridor.blurb: A northwest-facing wall tucked within the Cemetery crags at Horsemen's Center, near Apple Valley in the High Desert. Ten routes, eight bolted and two set for top-roping, are mostly steep to overhanging on dark patina-stained rock with good edges. Most fall in the 5.11 range, with a few 5.10s, one 5.9 and a 5.6 at the far end that works as a warm-up. All routes have chain anchors. It suits climbers already comfortable on hard sport routes who want some shade and a quiet corner of a busy area.
